title: Microsoft Edge: view sensitivity labels on MIP protected PDFs in the new PDF viewer
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, release-note evidence, permissions and policy references are supported. The registry reference is valid despite the automatic warning. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance on PDF-reader retirement and remove a checklist instruction whose control is not in the table.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans sensitivity-label viewing for MIP protected PDFs in Edge's new PDF viewer.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF to be well informed of the data classification to enable them to handle such sensitive documents. This change will be available in the new PDF viewer on Microsoft Edge.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes enterprise customers viewing classification information to handle sensitive documents appropriately.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF to be well informed of the data classification to enable them to handle such sensitive documents.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Edge"]

claims.claim: The roadmap still lists In development.

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on October 5, 2026, at the timestamp printed.
The Stable channel release notes already document sensitivity-label viewing in the new built-in PDF reader.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF to be well informed of the data classification to enable them to handle such sensitive documents. This change is available in the new Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader.

claims.claim: The cited sensitivity-label feature entry is under Stable version 138.0.3351.55.
That Stable release-note entry is dated June 26, 2025.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The sensitivity-label release note describes a controlled feature rollout, so visibility can differ between devices.
claims.quote: Note: This is a controlled feature rollout. If you don't see this feature, check back as we continue our rollout.

claims.claim: Edge can view MIP protected files saved locally.
claims.quote: With Microsoft Edge, users can view MIP protected files saved locally, or in the cloud. If saved locally, the file can be opened directly in the browser.

claims.claim: Edge can view MIP protected files saved in the cloud.
claims.quote: With Microsoft Edge, users can view MIP protected files saved locally, or in the cloud.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: A protected file opens in Edge if its signed-in profile has at least view permissions.
claims.quote: If the profile that the user is logged into Microsoft Edge with has at least view permissions to the file, the file will open in Microsoft Edge.

claims.claim: The new built-in PDF reader uses Adobe Acrobat's rendering engine.
claims.quote: The policy lets Microsoft Edge launch the new version of the built-in PDF reader that's powered by Adobe Acrobat's PDF rendering engine.

claims.claim: NewPDFReaderEnabled controls selection of the new Adobe-powered built-in PDF reader.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, Microsoft Edge will use the new Adobe Acrobat powered built-in PDF reader to open all PDF files.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify NewPDFReaderEnabled as a sensitivity-label-display setting or map this feature to that policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge PDF sensitivity label display default policy hide disable macOS NewPDFReaderEnabled. Read NewPDFReaderEnabled, Edge PDF reader, Edge policy list and Stable 138 release notes; these describe reader selection and label viewing, not a label-display policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The roadmap describes displaying an existing label, not new data access or changed protection permissions.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF to be well informed of the data classification to enable them to handle such sensitive documents.

claims.claim: The protected-PDF documentation lists work or school credentials as the supported Edge sign-in.
claims.quote: Supported sign-in credentials | Sign in to Edge with Work or school credentials.

claims.claim: The Edge PDF reader documentation says consumer identities are not supported for protected-file viewing.
claims.quote: Viewing files using consumer identities currently is not supported.

claims.claim: Rights restrictions come from the sensitivity label's encryption settings rather than merely displaying its name.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted, so that it: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes no autonomous action or sharing operation.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF to be well informed of the data classification to enable them to handle such sensitive documents.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: NewPDFReaderEnabled is deprecated starting in Edge 156.
claims.quote: Starting in Microsoft Edge version 156, this policy is deprecated as the built-in PDF reader experience has transitioned to the newer version.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The policy reference plans NewPDFReaderEnabled obsolescence starting in Edge 162.
claims.quote: The policy will remain supported for a minimum of 6 major releases and is planned to become obsolete starting in Microsoft Edge version 162.
claims.fix: Add to the retirement sentence: 'Microsoft's September 2026 PDF-partnership FAQ instead schedules removal of the legacy PDF engine in Edge 156.' Cite https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftedgeinsider/microsoft-edge-and-adobe-partner-to-improve-the-pdf-experience/3733481; its FAQ says 'The PDF engine in the Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader is scheduled to be removed in Edge version 156.' Keep the policy reference's 162 plan attributed to that reference.

claims.claim: Once obsolete, this policy can no longer be used to opt out of the new PDF reader.
claims.quote: Once obsolete, organizations will no longer be able to use this policy to opt out of the new PDF reader.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Edge PDF reader page says a licence is required for MIP and links Microsoft 365 licensing guidance.
claims.quote: A license is required for MIP. For more information, see this Microsoft 365 licensing guidance.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Administrators managing Information Protection features need appropriate licences.
claims.quote: This means the administrator creating and managing Information Protection features must have the appropriate licenses for the following subscription plans to configure the functionality.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: End users need appropriate licences for Information Protection functionality used in their client applications.
claims.quote: Similarly, end users also need the appropriate licenses to use the functionality in their respective client applications.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included within the product's existing MIP licensing, rather than a documented separate label-display entitlement.
claims.quote: A license is required for MIP. For more information, see this Microsoft 365 licensing guidance.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A licence or licence level specific to sensitivity-label display in Edge is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge MIP protected PDF sensitivity label display licensing price meter; Microsoft Edge sensitivity labels PDF license pricing. Read Edge PDF reader, Stable 138 notes, Microsoft 365 Security and Purview licensing: general MIP requirements, no display-specific licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate price for this label-display feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge MIP protected PDF sensitivity label display licensing price meter; Microsoft Edge sensitivity labels PDF license pricing. Read Edge PDF reader, Stable 138 notes, Purview service description and PDF-partnership FAQ; no label-display-specific price.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate meter for this feature, leaving administrative and communication time as the identified change cost.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge MIP protected PDF sensitivity label display licensing price meter; Microsoft Edge sensitivity labels PDF license pricing. Read Edge PDF reader, Stable 138 notes and Purview service description; no meter for viewing labels in Edge.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly published US Government availability for this label-display change.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge sensitivity label PDF viewing Worldwide GCC US Government availability. Read Stable 138 and 133 release-note excerpts: 133 documents protected-PDF opening including GCCH, not this label-display change; 138 gives no cloud-specific availability.

claims.claim: macOS coverage for this sensitivity-label-display feature is not explicitly published.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge sensitivity labels PDF macOS. Read protected-PDF readers, Edge PDF reader, NewPDFReaderEnabled, Stable 138 notes and Adobe-partnership FAQ. General protected-PDF opening supports Mac; the display entry names no OS, and the Adobe FAQ leaves Mac availability future.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state of sensitivity-label display itself is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge sensitivity PDF default policy; Microsoft Edge PDF sensitivity label display default policy hide disable macOS NewPDFReaderEnabled. Read Stable 138 notes, Edge PDF reader and policy reference. Stable 141 states the reader default, not the label-display default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no dedicated setting, UI or automation, to show or hide the label in the PDF viewer.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge PDF sensitivity label display default policy hide disable; Edge PDF sensitivity label hide. Read Edge policy list, PDF reader, NewPDFReaderEnabled and EdgeMipPdfEnabled. Reader-selection, iOS protected-file support and Office labeling controls are not label-display toggles.

claims.claim: Group Policy exposes the stated deprecated PDF-reader control under Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.
claims.quote: Group Policy (ADMX) info; GP name: Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader powered by Adobe Acrobat enabled (deprecated); GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.claim: The registry control is SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge with value NewPDFReaderEnabled of type REG_DWORD.
claims.quote: Registry settings; Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: NewPDFReaderEnabled; Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview can inventory sensitivity-labelled content to identify PDFs for testing.
claims.quote: Content explorer shows a current snapshot of the items that have a sensitivity label, a retention label, or are classified as a sensitive information type in your organization.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist instructs administrators to review label display names, but the controls table contains no sensitivity-label configuration control.
claims.quote: Review label display names for wording that would confuse users or disclose sensitive detail. | Table controls: Whether Edge uses the new Adobe Acrobat powered PDF reader (deprecated policy); A setting that shows or hides the sensitivity label in the PDF viewer.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Review label display names for wording that would confuse users or disclose sensitive detail.' Do not add a controls row.
